verses.1: Who has believed our message? And to whom has the arm of the LORD been revealed?
verses.2: He grew up before him like a tender shoot, a root out of parched ground. He had no stately form or majesty that we should look at him, nothing in his appearance that we should desire him.
verses.3: He was despised and rejected by men, a man of sorrows and familiar with suffering. He was like one from whom people hide their faces, and we held him in low esteem.
verses.4: Yet it was our sufferings he bore, and our sorrows he carried. Though we thought of him as stricken, smitten by God, and afflicted,
verses.5: he was pierced for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities. The punishment that brought us peace was upon him, and by his wounds we are healed.
verses.6: We all like sheep have gone astray, each of us has turned to his own way. The LORD has laid on him the iniquity of us all.
verses.7: He was offered because he himself chose to be, and he did not open his mouth. Like a lamb to the slaughter, and like a sheep before its shearers is silent, so he did not open his mouth.
verses.8: He was taken away, and who would have thought that he would be cut off from the land of the living, stricken for the transgression of my people?
verses.9: They made his grave with the wicked, and with the rich in death, though he had done no violence and had spoken no deceit.
verses.10: Yet it was the will of the LORD to crush him; he has put him to grief. When his life is poured out as an offering for guilt, he will see his descendants and prolong his days, and the will of the LORD will prosper in his hand.
verses.11: Out of his anguish he will see the light and be satisfied. My righteous servant will justify many by bearing their iniquities.
verses.12: Therefore I will give him a portion among the great, and he will divide the spoil with the strong, because he surrendered himself to death, and was counted among the wicked, yet he bore the sin of many and made intercession for the transgressors.

notes:
Notes
- v. 10: "When his life is poured out as an offering for guilt" reflects the Hebrew "עֲשָׂה אָשָׁם נַפְשׁוֹ" (asah asham naphsho), which literally means "he made his life a guilt offering." This rendering preserves the meaning without adopting the Septuagint's "περὶ ἁμαρτίας" (for sin).
- v. 11: "Out of his anguish he will see the light and be satisfied" translates "מֵעֲמַל נַפְשׁוֹ יִרְאֶה יִשְׂבָּע בְּדַעְתּוֹ" (me'amal naphsho yir'eh yisba' be'da'ato). The exact meaning of "בְּדַעְתּוֹ" (be-da'ato) is uncertain; "be satisfied in knowledge" or "in understanding" is a plausible interpretation, but "be satisfied" is chosen as the clearest and most natural rendering.
raw:
[1] Who has believed our message? And to whom has the arm of the LORD been revealed?

[2] He grew up before him like a tender shoot, a root out of parched ground. He had no stately form or majesty that we should look at him, nothing in his appearance that we should desire him.

[3] He was despised and rejected by men, a man of sorrows and familiar with suffering. He was like one from whom people hide their faces, and we held him in low esteem.

[4] Yet it was our sufferings he bore, and our sorrows he carried. Though we thought of him as stricken, smitten by God, and afflicted,

[5] he was pierced for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities. The punishment that brought us peace was upon him, and by his wounds we are healed.

[6] We all like sheep have gone astray, each of us has turned to his own way. The LORD has laid on him the iniquity of us all.

[7] He was offered because he himself chose to be, and he did not open his mouth. Like a lamb to the slaughter, and like a sheep before its shearers is silent, so he did not open his mouth.

[8] He was taken away, and who would have thought that he would be cut off from the land of the living, stricken for the transgression of my people?

[9] They made his grave with the wicked, and with the rich in death, though he had done no violence and had spoken no deceit.

[10] Yet it was the will of the LORD to crush him; he has put him to grief. When his life is poured out as an offering for guilt, he will see his descendants and prolong his days, and the will of the LORD will prosper in his hand.

[11] Out of his anguish he will see the light and be satisfied. My righteous servant will justify many by bearing their iniquities.

[12] Therefore I will give him a portion among the great, and he will divide the spoil with the strong, because he surrendered himself to death, and was counted among the wicked, yet he bore the sin of many and made intercession for the transgressors.

---
Notes
- v. 10: "When his life is poured out as an offering for guilt" reflects the Hebrew "עֲשָׂה אָשָׁם נַפְשׁוֹ" (asah asham naphsho), which literally means "he made his life a guilt offering." This rendering preserves the meaning without adopting the Septuagint's "περὶ ἁμαρτίας" (for sin).
- v. 11: "Out of his anguish he will see the light and be satisfied" translates "מֵעֲמַל נַפְשׁוֹ יִרְאֶה יִשְׂבָּע בְּדַעְתּוֹ" (me'amal naphsho yir'eh yisba' be'da'ato). The exact meaning of "בְּדַעְתּוֹ" (be-da'ato) is uncertain; "be satisfied in knowledge" or "in understanding" is a plausible interpretation, but "be satisfied" is chosen as the clearest and most natural rendering.
